definitions.explanation: Words that indirectly express criticism or displeasure, often through irony or insinuation.
An attitude or behavior that makes others feel uncomfortable.

examples.japanese: {嫌味|いやみ}を{言|い}われて{傷|きず}ついた。
examples.english: I was hurt by a snide remark.

examples.japanese: それは{嫌味|いやみ}で{言|い}っているのか？
{上司|じょうし}に{嫌味|いやみ}を{言|い}われるのはつらい。
examples.english: It's tough to be on the receiving end of snide remarks from your boss.

examples.japanese: {嫌味|いやみ}な{言|い}い{方|かた}をする{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: They have an unpleasant way of speaking.

examples.japanese: {嫌味|いやみ}な{態度|たいど}を{取|と}らないでください。
examples.english: Please don't act in such an unpleasant manner.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{嫌味|いやみ}なく{自慢話|じまんばなし}ができるから、みんなに{好|す}かれている。
examples.english: That person can brag without being unpleasant about it, so everyone likes them.

notes:
FORMATION:
{嫌|いや} (unpleasant) + {味|み} (flavor/quality)

Literally 'unpleasant taste/quality.'

ADJECTIVE USAGE:
{嫌味|いやみ}な + noun - unpleasant, disagreeable
・{嫌味|いやみ}な{人|ひと} - unpleasant person
・{嫌味|いやみ}な{言|い}い{方|かた} - snide way of speaking

COLLOCATIONS:
・{嫌味|いやみ}を{言|い}う - to make a snide remark
・{嫌味|いやみ}ったらしい - full of sarcasm
・{嫌味|いやみ}に{聞|き}こえる - to sound sarcastic
・{嫌味|いやみ}なく - without being unpleasant
